posterior_text: Task Goal: Help the user cancel an existing reservation booking. Observed Procedure: - Asked the user for required cancellation details: user ID, reservation ID, and cancellation reason. - Retrieved the reservation details for the provided user/reservation pair (EHGLP3 / emma_kim_9957) via a reservation lookup tool. - Summarized the booking (route, date, cabin, passengers, insurance, booking time, payment) and asked eligibility-confirming questions (airline-cancelled segments or business cabin). - Determined the booking was not eligible for a refundable cancellation given: booked >24 hours ago, no airline cancellation, basic economy, no insurance, and “change of plan.” - Offered to proceed with cancellation without refund, but the user did not accept. - When the user asserted prior insurance guidance, explained eligibility could only be based on the current booking record and offered transfer to a human agent for review. - Executed transfer to a human agent after user confirmation. Validated Facts: - User requested to cancel a booking. - User provided user ID emma_kim_9957 and reservation ID EHGLP3; reason: change of plan. - Reservation lookup returned a one-way PHX → JFK via SEA on 2024-05-17, basic economy, 2 passengers, insurance “no,” created at 2024-05-04T23:12:06, payment amount $208, and payment_id credit_card_5832574. - User confirmed no airline cancellation and all segments in basic economy. - The assistant stated the reservation was not eligible for refund/credit under the rules it could apply. - User requested transfer to a human agent; tool reported “Transfer successful.” Failure/Success Pivot: Success pivot: The agent correctly identified that automated refund/credit was not supported based on the booking attributes and escalated to a human agent when the user requested an exception review. Missing Step or Critical Decision: Critical decision: Whether to proceed with cancellation without refund versus escalation; the user declined cancellation without refund and requested escalation, leading to transfer rather than cancellation. Reusable Lesson: When refund eligibility is constrained by the booking record (e.g., no insurance, basic economy, >24 hours, no airline cancellation), clearly state limitations, avoid committing to exceptions, and offer a human-agent transfer for disputes or special claims. Candidate Workflow Signal: collect_request -> gather_identifiers -> retrieve_reservation -> validate_refund_eligibility -> communicate_options -> escalate_to_human_agent

workflow.precondition: User requests to cancel an existing reservation; assistant can access a reservation lookup tool and (optionally) a human-agent transfer tool.
critical_checks: Confirm user_id and reservation_id match a retrieved reservation before discussing policy outcomes
Verify refund eligibility inputs from record and user (booking age >24h, airline-cancelled segments, cabin/fare type, travel insurance presence)
Do not promise refunds/credits when the booking record does not support eligibility; clearly state limits of automated handling
Before cancelling, confirm user consent to any non-refundable outcome; if disputed, offer escalation
workflow.commit_gate: User explicitly confirms they want to proceed with cancellation after being told the expected refund/credit outcome (including $0 refund if ineligible).
workflow.postcondition: Either (a) cancellation is executed with the agreed refund/credit outcome, or (b) the case is transferred to a human agent for exception/dispute review without performing cancellation.
tool_hints: Use reservation lookup tool with (user_id, reservation_id) to fetch itinerary, fare/cabin, passengers, insurance flag, booking timestamp, and payment details
Use human-agent transfer tool when user disputes eligibility, cites prior guidance not reflected in the record, or requests an exception review
